lens: ornament and elevating elements vs top-agency menu work
top_problem: The right column runs out of content after Dry Cider, leaving about 84 pt of dead cream above Wine (Beer ends near y444 while Cocktails ends at y492). Because of that, the space above section headers is uneven (36 pt on the left, 84 pt on the right) and the CIDER subheader (y396) sits 12 pt off HOUSE ORIGINALS (y384) across the columns. The ornament is also weighted almost entirely at the top and bottom edges: a strong papel picado banner, then a body that is a plain list with no signature moment.
fixes: Balance the columns: move Beer's 84 pt surplus into the body. Either set the Beer column's item gap so Beer ends at y492, or bring in a small agave-and-diamond spot ornament or a 'Draft rotates, ask your server' note set on the grid, so the space above Wine matches the 36 pt above Spirits and the right column has no dead patch.
Line up the second subheaders across columns so CIDER shares the y384 row with HOUSE ORIGINALS, the same way AGAVE/BY THE GLASS and BRANDY/SPARKLING already share rows.

Give House Originals one signature treatment a top agency would use: a thin terracotta or marigold framed panel or a cut-paper corner motif around its two items. This puts the high-margin drinks in a prime spot and carries the banner's language into the body instead of leaving the ornament only at the edges.

Soften the banner's visual weight against the quiet body: cut it to 7 flags or reduce their height by about 15 percent, keep the green and marigold flags out of terracotta at the ends so the colours alternate, and repeat one flag motif small beside each Spanish kicker in place of the plain diamond.

Add one subtle material cue across the whole page, such as a 3-4 percent paper-fibre texture or a hairline cut-paper scallop on the footer rules. That ties the banner, the agave footer and the dotted gold column divider into one crafted system rather than separate clip-art pieces.

Separately, half the menu (every beer, cider, wine and spirit) has only a one-line generic description, such as 'Sparkling.' or 'Dry red wine.', with no ABV, region or producer. All of these are flagged in missing_ingredients, but the menu still reads thin.

Balance the second column: the empty block under Cider (about 130 pt) should be filled by moving the section break or evening the vertical spacing, so both columns end together without a dead zone in the right column.

Put House Originals (Brown Butter Old Fashioned, House Daiquiri) in the first slot under Cocktails, or give the signature drinks a visible mark, so the highest-margin, venue-specific drinks sit in the prime top-left spot ahead of the generic Manhattan.

Get ABV and style for the 3 beers and the cider, region for Malbec and Pinot Grigio, region or method for Brut Rosé, and glass/bottle pour labels, and print them as soon as they are supplied; until then, keep the flags and do not write filler text such as 'Sparkling.' that adds no facts.

top_problem: The descriptions are in two different voices. The cocktails get full recipe-card lines (for example 'Stirred, served up in a coupe.'), while the beer, cider and wine get one- or two-word labels such as 'Dry red wine.', 'Dry white wine.' and 'Sparkling.' On the phone the lower half reads like a stock list. Separately, the draft item Junmai Ginjo (phg.menu_items 57617f46, $12) is not printed: 15 draft rows, 14 rendered. Checked against the recipe rows: the glass, garnish and method for Margarita (rocks / lime wheel / shaken over fresh ice), Manhattan (coupe / cocktail cherry / stirred), Brown Butter Old Fashioned (rocks / orange peel / large cube) and House Daiquiri (coupe / lime coin / shaken) all match phg.recipe_versions through menu_items.current_recipe_version_id (items 14555870, bf732e78, 0cc4e912, 44dcba6e). The Manhattan's printed line leaves out the 'aromatic bitters' that are in its draft menu_description (bf732e78) and in the standard spec in cocktail_reference ('2 dashes Angostura'). The spirit claims 'D.O. Tequila', 'aged at least one year in oak' (Añejo, 124f8949) and 'aged at least four years in oak' (Cognac VSOP, 75501d63) appear in neither the draft descriptions nor any recipe row; I did not check spirit_lexicon for them.
fixes: Rewrite the beer, cider and wine descriptions to the cocktail length in the same voice, using only facts from the draft (e.g. Pinot Grigio 'Crisp, dry white', and give Dry Cider a full sentence instead of the fragment 'Sparkling.'), and flag missing_ingredients to get grape region and beer ABV rather than printing class labels like 'Dry red wine.'
Restore 'aromatic bitters' in the Manhattan line ('Rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters; cocktail cherry.') to match draft item bf732e78 and the cocktail_reference spec.
Find a public.spirit_lexicon row for the Añejo 'one year in oak', VSOP 'four years in oak' and 'D.O. Tequila' claims and cite it, or cut them back to the draft wording.

Layout note for the designer: print the missing Junmai Ginjo ($12), add pour labels to Spirits and Draft (e.g. '2 oz', '16 oz') the way Wine has 'By the glass', and use one description measure throughout (the Añejo line breaks early and leaves 'oak.' on a short second line, while Margarita's lines run the full width).
